project.title: Spooky Monopoly
project.summary: A single-player browser property game with local token unlocks and optional shared statistics.

items.title: Verify the results flow against a configured Supabase project
items.notes: Phase 2 (Next). A disposable local Supabase stack passed the empty aggregate, one completed-game insert, and overall and Human-group totals with a public key. The legacy routes also worked. The check-shared-stats.mjs command repeats those checks and stops before insertion when the table already reports games. The setup-shared-stats.sql script creates the initial table for a fresh project. A disposable Supabase Postgres database verified the exact script, including public reads and inserts, denied public updates and deletes, property-count constraints, and preservation of the existing row when setup is repeated. Apply the setup to a hosted test project, run the smoke check, and confirm the hosted constraints and policies before changing shared writes or aggregation. Keep local play independent of this check.

items.title: Validate submissions and show confirmed aggregates
items.notes: Phase 2 (Next). The results screen checks the HTTP response and refreshes shared statistics after the server confirms the submission. Chromium covers delayed confirmation, a failed submission, disabled statistics, and local restart. Validate result fields at runtime in the submit handler after checking the hosted table contract. Introduce a backward-compatible submission ID and a database uniqueness rule once the live schema is confirmed. Verify aggregates across response pages and confirm that a retried submission leaves local play available.

items.title: Define and test the two-seat match rules
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 1 (supervised two-player pilot). Record the contract in docs/multiplayer-rules.md before changing the engine. Prototype equal human seats, random first seat, and 10 rounds with one turn per player per round. Define legal Buy and Pass actions for unowned properties. Test posted rent transferred to the owner on landing, capped by the payer’s cash, with both players remaining through the last round. Score cash plus owned property purchase value and allow ties. Include worked examples for unaffordable rent, a purchase, and a tie. Playtest first-seat advantage before tuning rent and pacing. The proposed pilot contract and test scenarios are in docs/multiplayer-rules.md. The pilot rules have executable tests. A paired simulation over 1,000 roll sequences gave the first seat 1,114 wins out of 2,000 matches (55.7%). The local playtest command uses the pilot engine to run a controlled pair with identical rolls and swapped starters. Scripted inputs verified complete reports with scores, property ownership, rent, and feedback. Human playtesting and any balance tuning are still pending.

items.title: Add multiplayer games with shared turns
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 2 (private release). Release the private two-player mode once the supervised pilot, authoritative turns, phone-sized board, and reconnect and leave flow are verified. Two separate browser profiles must join, reconnect, and finish the same match without duplicate turns or divergent results. Preserve standalone solo play and keep multiplayer results separate from solo aggregates. Measure invite-to-first-roll time, pilot completion, and the share of interrupted matches that resume to completion.

items.title: Support private matches for three to four players
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 3 (expansion). Build on the private two-seat release. Extend the seat model and layout, then playtest equal seats at each room size before changing faction rules. Check wait time, competition for property, and round count. Verify all four seats receive the intended number of turns and a reconnect restores the same seat. Compare match completion by room size.

items.title: Make faction differences playable in multiplayer
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 3 (expansion). Use the equal-seat baseline and larger-room playtests before introducing faction variants. Document legal actions and objectives before match start. Test vampire acquisition advantages and an elf objective that recognises resistance rather than relying on the standard wealth score. Verify each enabled faction has a reachable objective and keep equal-seat play available.

items.title: Show the shared history of rent and ownership
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 3 (expansion). Build on stable player and property IDs and the recorded action history. Highlight actual rent transfers, later purchases, and changes in ownership. Distinguish observed transfers from illustrative links about how pooled cash funded another action. Verify the recap matches recorded transactions and final balances and is readable on a phone. Measure rematches after players view the result.
